title: Museum guide training
text: You are training to be a guide at a science museum. Listen to your manager and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Welcome to the science museum.
explanation: Stress 'science' and 'museum'; the 'to the' in the middle is quick and unstressed.

stem: Please keep your group together at all times.
explanation: Link 'keep your' and 'at all' smoothly, and keep the final phrase 'at all times' intact.

stem: The dinosaur exhibit is on the second floor this month.
explanation: Say all three syllables of 'dinosaur' and keep the time phrase 'this month' at the end.

stem: Visitors who have a timed ticket can enter the planetarium first.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who have a timed ticket' together; 'timed ticket' has two clear t sounds.

stem: Before the tour starts, remind everyone to turn off the flash on their cameras.
explanation: Pause briefly after the time clause 'Before the tour starts', then link 'turn off' into one sound.

stem: If a child gets separated from the group, bring them to the information desk near the entrance.
explanation: Keep the 'if' clause first and the place phrase 'near the entrance' at the very end; stress 'information desk'.

stem: Each tour lasts about forty-five minutes, and you should finish in the hall where the moon rock is displayed.
explanation: Say 'forty-five' clearly and keep the relative clause 'where the moon rock is displayed' in order after 'hall'.

title: Library assistant training
text: You have a new part-time job as an assistant at the university library. Listen to the head librarian and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Thanks for joining us today.
explanation: Link 'joining us' so it sounds like 'joining-gus', and stress 'today'.

stem: Your first shift starts at eight on Monday.
explanation: Watch the cluster in 'first shift'; keep both the 'st' and the 'sh' sounds.

stem: Returned books go on the gray cart behind the counter.
explanation: The '-ed' in 'returned' is a soft d sound; stress 'gray cart' and 'counter'.

stem: Students can borrow up to ten books with their campus card.
explanation: Link 'up to' and say the number 'ten' clearly; keep 'with their campus card' at the end.

stem: The quiet study rooms on the third floor must be booked a day ahead.
explanation: Do not mix up 'quiet' and 'quite'; 'quiet' has two syllables. Keep 'must be booked' as a passive.

stem: When someone asks for a journal article, show them how to search the online database first.
explanation: Start with the time clause 'When someone asks', and keep 'how to search' together before 'the online database'.

stem: Any laptop that is left at a table for more than an hour should be taken to the front desk.
explanation: Hold the long subject 'Any laptop that is left at a table' together before the verb 'should be taken'.

title: Hotel front desk
text: You are starting work at the front desk of a city hotel. Listen to the shift supervisor and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Always greet guests with a smile.
explanation: Link 'greet guests' without adding an extra vowel, and stress 'smile'.

stem: Check-in begins at three in the afternoon.
explanation: Stress 'three' and 'afternoon'; 'begins' ends in a z sound.

stem: Breakfast is served in the garden room until ten thirty.
explanation: Say 'breakfast' as two syllables, 'brek-fust', and keep the time 'ten thirty' clear.

stem: Guests who arrive late can collect their keys from the night manager.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who arrive late' right after 'Guests'; stress 'night manager'.

stem: If the printer stops working, call the technician on extension two one four.
explanation: Read the extension as single digits, 'two one four', and pause slightly after the 'if' clause.

stem: After a guest checks out, let housekeeping know so they can prepare the room quickly.
explanation: Watch the cluster in 'checks out'; keep 'let housekeeping know' in that word order.

stem: Remember that the airport shuttle leaves from the side entrance every hour, starting at six in the morning.
explanation: Stress 'airport shuttle' and 'every hour'; keep the final phrase 'starting at six in the morning' complete.

title: Botanical garden volunteer
text: You are volunteering at a botanical garden for the summer. Listen to the volunteer coordinator and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Please wear gloves when weeding.
explanation: Stress 'gloves' and 'weeding'; the 'w' sounds in 'wear' and 'when' need rounded lips.

stem: The rose garden opens to visitors at nine.
explanation: Link 'opens to' and keep the plural z sound in 'visitors'.

stem: Water the herb beds early, before the sun gets hot.
explanation: In American English 'herb' starts with no h sound, 'erb'. Pause lightly before 'before the sun gets hot'.

stem: The tools you need are kept in the shed by the pond.
explanation: Keep 'the tools you need' together as the subject; stress 'shed' and 'pond'.

stem: Visitors often ask about the cactus house, which is next to the main greenhouse.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'which is next to the main greenhouse' after 'cactus house'; stress 'often' lightly.

stem: When you finish pruning, put the cuttings in the compost bins behind the visitor center.
explanation: Start with the time clause 'When you finish pruning'; keep the final place phrase 'behind the visitor center' together.

stem: On Saturday afternoon, we're leading a family walk through the tropical section, so we'll need at least four extra helpers.
explanation: Say the contractions 'we're' and 'we'll' naturally, and keep 'at least four extra helpers' in order at the end.

title: Orientation leader
text: You are training to be an orientation leader for new students at a university. Listen to the student life director and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Orientation week starts on Tuesday.
explanation: Stress the 'a' in 'orientation', and link 'starts on' smoothly.

stem: Each leader will guide a group of twelve.
explanation: Keep the 'will' contraction-free here and say 'twelve' with a clear final v sound.

stem: Meet your group outside the student union at ten.
explanation: Link 'meet your' into 'mee-chur', a natural American linking; stress 'student union'.

stem: Show new students where the dining hall and health center are.
explanation: This is an indirect question, so the verb 'are' comes last; do not move it to after 'where'.

stem: Some international students arrive late, so check the list again every evening.
explanation: Stress 'international' on the third syllable, 'in-ter-NA-tion-al', and keep 'every evening' at the end.

stem: If anyone feels unwell during the campus tour, call the number printed on your badge.
explanation: Keep the 'if' clause first, and say 'printed on your badge' as one phrase after 'number'.

stem: By the end of the week, every student should know how to log in to the course portal and find their timetable.
explanation: Keep 'how to log in' together and stress the last item, 'timetable'; there is no pause after 'portal'.

title: Restaurant kitchen
text: You have just started working in the kitchen of a busy restaurant. Listen to the head chef and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Wash your hands before every shift.
explanation: Keep the sh sound in both 'wash' and 'shift', and stress 'every'.

stem: Clean knives go back on the magnetic strip.
explanation: The k in 'knives' is silent; stress 'magnetic' on the second syllable.

stem: Fresh vegetables are delivered every morning around six thirty.
explanation: Say 'vegetables' as three syllables, 'VEJ-tuh-bulz', and keep the time 'six thirty' clear.

stem: Label every container with the date and what is inside it.
explanation: Keep 'what is inside it' as an indirect phrase, with no question order; stress 'label' and 'date'.

stem: The walk-in fridge must stay below four degrees, so close the door quickly.
explanation: The l in 'walk' is silent; say 'four degrees' clearly and link 'close the door'.

stem: When a customer mentions a nut allergy, tell the server and use a separate cutting board.
explanation: Start with the time clause 'When a customer mentions a nut allergy'; stress 'separate' on the first syllable.

stem: Before you leave at night, make sure the ovens are off and the floor near the dishwasher has been mopped.
explanation: Keep both parts after 'make sure' in order, and say the passive 'has been mopped' as one quick phrase.

title: Cycling tour guide
text: You are training to lead bicycle tours of a riverside city. Listen to the tour company owner and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Check every helmet before we leave.
explanation: Stress 'every' and 'leave'; the t in 'helmet' is light before 'before'.

stem: Riders should stay in a single line.
explanation: Link 'stay in a' smoothly and stress 'single line'.

stem: Our first stop is the old stone bridge downtown.
explanation: Keep the three adjectives in order, 'old stone bridge', and stress 'downtown' on the second syllable.

stem: Always use hand signals whenever you need to turn left or right.
explanation: Watch the cluster in 'hand signals'; link 'turn left' without an extra vowel.

stem: The river path is narrow, so ring your bell before passing anyone.
explanation: Separate the r and l sounds in 'ring' and 'bell', and keep 'before passing anyone' at the end.

stem: After the lunch break at the market, we ride north to Harbor Park for photos.
explanation: Keep the time phrase 'After the lunch break at the market' first, and say the place name 'Harbor Park' as one unit.

stem: If a tire goes flat, the repair kit is in the red bag that's clipped under your seat.
explanation: Say the contraction 'that's' quickly, and keep 'clipped under your seat' together at the end.

title: Zoo keeper assistant
text: You are starting a summer job helping the keepers at a city zoo. Listen to the senior keeper and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Never feed the animals yourself.
explanation: Stress 'never' strongly; it carries the meaning of the instruction.

stem: The penguins are fed twice a day.
explanation: Keep the passive 'are fed'; link 'twice a day' into one smooth phrase.

stem: Lock both gates when you leave an enclosure.
explanation: Link 'both gates' and say the final t in 'gates'; stress 'lock' and 'both'.

stem: The giraffes get nervous when there are loud noises nearby.
explanation: The g in 'giraffes' sounds like j; stress the second syllable, 'ji-RAFFS'.

stem: You'll spend your first week in the reptile house with a keeper named Kwame.
explanation: Say 'You'll' as one syllable and keep the phrase 'with a keeper named Kwame' after 'reptile house'.

stem: Write down how much each animal eats, because the vet checks those records every Friday.
explanation: Keep 'how much each animal eats' in statement order, and link 'checks those' carefully.

stem: While visitors are watching the sea lion show, stay behind the yellow line and keep the bucket of fish closed.
explanation: Begin with the time clause 'While visitors are watching the sea lion show'; keep the two instructions joined by 'and'.

title: Bookstore clerk
text: You have been hired to work at an independent bookstore near a college. Listen to the store owner and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: New arrivals go by the window.
explanation: Link 'new arrivals' and stress 'window'; 'go by' is quick.

stem: We open at ten on weekdays.
explanation: Link 'open at' into 'o-pen-at' and stress 'ten' and 'weekdays'.

stem: Textbooks for the fall semester are in the back room.
explanation: Stress 'textbooks' on the first syllable and say 'fall semester' as one phrase.

stem: Customers who order online can pick up their books at the register.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who order online' after 'Customers'; 'pick up' links into one sound.

stem: If a title isn't on the shelf, check whether it's on order.
explanation: Keep both negatives and contractions, 'isn't' and 'it's', and keep 'whether it's on order' in statement word order.

stem: Every Thursday evening, a local author reads in the café, so we put out thirty chairs.
explanation: Watch the th sounds in 'Thursday' and 'thirty'; keep the time phrase 'Every Thursday evening' at the start.

stem: Students who show a valid ID get ten percent off, but the discount doesn't apply to magazines.
explanation: Say 'I-D' as two letters and 'ten percent' clearly; stress 'doesn't' in the contrast after 'but'.

title: Fitness center staff
text: You are training to work at the front desk of the campus fitness center. Listen to the center manager and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Ask every member to swipe in.
explanation: Link 'swipe in' into 'swy-pin' and stress 'every'.

stem: Towels are in the cabinet behind you.
explanation: Say 'towels' as two syllables, 'TOW-ulz', and stress 'behind'.

stem: The pool closes for cleaning every Wednesday at noon.
explanation: Keep 'for cleaning' after 'closes', and stress 'Wednesday', which has two syllables, 'WENZ-day'.

stem: Members who want a personal trainer should fill out this form.
explanation: Hold the relative clause 'who want a personal trainer' together before 'should'; link 'fill out'.

stem: Remind people to wipe down the machines after they finish their workout.
explanation: Keep the time clause 'after they finish their workout' at the end; link 'wipe down' cleanly.

stem: The yoga class on the second floor fills up fast, so suggest signing up online.
explanation: Stress 'fast' and 'online'; 'fills up' and 'signing up' both link into one sound.

stem: If someone feels dizzy on a treadmill, help them sit down and call the first aid number by the door.
explanation: Begin with the 'if' clause and keep 'the first aid number by the door' together at the end.

title: Art gallery attendant
text: You are training to be an attendant at an art gallery. Listen to the gallery supervisor and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Please don't touch the paintings.
explanation: Stress 'don't' and 'touch'; the t at the end of 'don't' is very light.

stem: The gallery is free on Sunday mornings.
explanation: Say 'gallery' as three syllables and keep the plural in 'mornings'.

stem: Large bags must be left in the lockers downstairs.
explanation: Keep the passive 'must be left', and link 'left in' smoothly.

stem: The portrait room is the one with the dark blue walls.
explanation: Stress 'portrait' on the first syllable and keep 'dark blue walls' in that order.

stem: Visitors may take photos, but they can't use a flash or a tripod.
explanation: Stress 'can't' in the contrast after 'but', and say 'tripod' as 'TRY-pod'.

stem: When a school group arrives, walk them to the sculpture garden before the crowds come in.
explanation: The 'ch' in 'school' sounds like k. Keep the opening time clause and the final phrase 'before the crowds come in'.

stem: The new exhibition, which opens next Friday, features landscapes that were painted by artists from northern Europe.
explanation: Keep the inserted clause 'which opens next Friday' between commas, then continue with 'features landscapes'; stress 'northern Europe'.

title: Chemistry lab assistant
text: You have a job as a lab assistant in a university chemistry department. Listen to the lab coordinator and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Safety glasses are required here.
explanation: Stress 'safety' and 'required'; 'glasses are' links into 'glass-ez-are'.

stem: Your lab coat hangs by the door.
explanation: Watch the final s in 'hangs', and keep the place phrase 'by the door' at the end.

stem: Set up the microscopes before the first class arrives.
explanation: Link 'set up' into 'seh-dup' and keep the time clause 'before the first class arrives'.

stem: Glass containers go in the blue bin, not the regular trash.
explanation: Stress 'blue' and 'not' to show the contrast; 'regular' has three syllables.

stem: Students who spill any chemicals must report it to the instructor right away.
explanation: The 'ch' in 'chemicals' sounds like k; keep the relative clause 'who spill any chemicals' together.

stem: After each session, count the beakers and write the total on the sheet by the sink.
explanation: Start with 'After each session', and keep both actions in order: count, then write.

stem: The fire extinguisher is next to the emergency shower, and everyone should know where it is on their first day.
explanation: Stress 'extinguisher' on the second syllable, and keep 'where it is' in statement order.

title: Airport information desk
text: You are starting work at the information desk of an international airport. Listen to your team leader and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Good morning, how can I help?
explanation: Use a friendly rising tone on 'help' and link 'can I' into 'ka-nai'.

stem: Gates twenty to forty are in Terminal B.
explanation: Say the numbers 'twenty' and 'forty' clearly, and stress the letter 'B' at the end.

stem: The train to the city center leaves every fifteen minutes.
explanation: Stress 'fifteen' on the second syllable so it is not heard as 'fifty'.

stem: Passengers with connecting flights should follow the orange signs upstairs.
explanation: Keep 'with connecting flights' after 'Passengers', and say 'orange' as two syllables.

stem: Lost luggage is handled by the airline office next to baggage claim.
explanation: Watch the l sounds in 'lost luggage' and keep the passive 'is handled by' together.

stem: If a flight is delayed for more than two hours, give the passenger a meal voucher.
explanation: Keep the 'if' clause first and say 'more than two hours' as one phrase; stress 'meal voucher'.

stem: Travelers who need a wheelchair can wait at the blue seats while we call someone from customer service.
explanation: Hold the relative clause 'who need a wheelchair' together, and keep the 'while' clause at the end.

title: Summer camp counselor
text: You are training to be a counselor at a summer camp by a lake. Listen to the camp director and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Campers arrive on Sunday afternoon.
explanation: Link 'arrive on' into 'a-ry-von' and stress 'Sunday afternoon'.

stem: Each cabin has eight beds and one counselor.
explanation: Say 'eight beds' without dropping the t, and keep 'and one counselor' at the end.

stem: Swimming is only allowed when a lifeguard is on duty.
explanation: Stress 'only', and keep the time clause 'when a lifeguard is on duty' complete.

stem: Make sure everyone puts on sunscreen before the morning hike begins.
explanation: Link 'puts on' and keep 'before the morning hike begins' as one time clause.

stem: The dining hall bell rings at seven, and breakfast is served at seven fifteen.
explanation: Say 'seven' and 'seven fifteen' clearly; stress 'fifteen' on the second syllable.

stem: Children who feel homesick can talk to the camp nurse, whose cabin is near the flagpole.
explanation: There are two relative clauses, 'who feel homesick' and 'whose cabin is near the flagpole'; keep both in place.

stem: On the last evening, each group performs a short skit around the campfire, so start practicing with your cabin by Wednesday.
explanation: Keep the time phrases 'On the last evening' and 'by Wednesday' in their places; link 'each group' smoothly.

title: Walking tour guide
text: You are learning to give walking tours of an old harbor town. Listen to the senior guide and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Our tour begins at the lighthouse.
explanation: Stress 'lighthouse' on the first syllable, 'LIGHT-house'.

stem: Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestone streets.
explanation: Say 'comfortable' as three syllables, 'KUMF-ter-bul', and link 'cobblestone streets'.

stem: The fish market has been open for two hundred years.
explanation: Keep 'has been open' together, and say 'two hundred years' clearly.

stem: Point out the blue house where the town's first mayor lived.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'where the town's first mayor lived' after 'blue house'; watch the cluster in 'first'.

stem: If it rains, take the group into the maritime museum on Bay Street.
explanation: Stress 'maritime' on the first syllable, and keep the street name 'Bay Street' at the end.

stem: Most visitors want to see the old shipyard, which is a ten-minute walk along the water.
explanation: Say 'ten-minute' as one unit, and keep the 'which' clause after 'old shipyard'.

stem: Before you finish the tour, recommend a café on Harbor Square and mention that the ferry leaves at four.
explanation: Begin with the time clause, keep 'Harbor Square' as a place name, and say the final number 'four' clearly.

title: Aquarium educator
text: You are training to be an educator at a public aquarium. Listen to the education manager and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Please don't tap on the glass.
explanation: Stress 'don't' and 'glass'; link 'tap on' into 'ta-pon'.

stem: The shark tunnel is through those doors.
explanation: Watch the th sounds in 'through' and 'those'; they are different, one voiceless and one voiced.

stem: Feeding time for the sea otters is at eleven.
explanation: Link 'sea otters' smoothly and say 'eleven' with stress on the second syllable.

stem: Children can touch the starfish in the shallow pool by the café.
explanation: Say 'starfish' as one word with stress on 'star', and keep 'by the café' at the end.

stem: Explain that the jellyfish have no brain, but they can still sense light.
explanation: Keep the 'that' clause together and stress 'no brain' and 'still' to show the contrast.

stem: When a school group visits, start with the coral reef tank and finish at the penguin beach.
explanation: Begin with the time clause, then keep the order 'start with' and 'finish at'; link 'coral reef' clearly with two r sounds.

stem: The sea turtle we rescued last spring is getting stronger, and we hope to return her to the ocean in June.
explanation: Keep the reduced relative clause 'we rescued last spring' after 'sea turtle', and end with 'in June'.

title: Student newspaper intern
text: You have joined the campus newspaper as an intern. Listen to the editor and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Deadlines are every Thursday at noon.
explanation: Stress 'deadlines' on the first syllable and say the th in 'Thursday' clearly.

stem: Always check the spelling of people's names.
explanation: Keep the possessive 's in 'people's', and stress 'always' and 'names'.

stem: Our staff meeting is in room two oh five.
explanation: Read the room number as Americans say it, 'two oh five', and stress 'staff meeting'.

stem: Record every interview, but ask permission before you start the recorder.
explanation: The noun 'recorder' is stressed on the second syllable, and the verb 'record' here is also 're-CORD'.

stem: The sports section needs someone who can cover the basketball game on Saturday.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who can cover the basketball game' after 'someone'; watch the cluster in 'sports section'.

stem: If you take photos at an event, write down the names of everyone in the picture.
explanation: Keep the 'if' clause first and link 'write down'; stress 'everyone'.

stem: Once your article has been edited, read it one more time and send it back to me by Friday morning.
explanation: Keep the passive 'has been edited' in the time clause, and end with the deadline 'by Friday morning'.

title: Theater usher
text: You are training to work as an usher at a city theater. Listen to the house manager and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Doors open thirty minutes early.
explanation: Watch the th in 'thirty' and stress 'early'.

stem: Check each ticket and point to the seat.
explanation: Link 'check each' and say the final t in 'seat' lightly.

stem: Programs are on the table next to the coat check.
explanation: Stress 'programs' on the first syllable and say 'coat check' as one phrase.

stem: People who arrive late must wait until the first scene ends.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who arrive late' together, and say 'scene' with a long e.

stem: During the show, use your flashlight only to help guests find their rows.
explanation: Start with 'During the show', and stress 'only' because it limits the instruction.

stem: The intermission lasts fifteen minutes, and the bar in the upper lobby will be open.
explanation: Stress 'intermission' on the third syllable, and keep 'in the upper lobby' after 'the bar'.

stem: If a fire alarm sounds, stay calm and guide everyone to the nearest exit, which is marked with a green light.
explanation: Keep the 'if' clause first and the 'which' clause after 'nearest exit'; link 'stay calm' smoothly.

title: Farmers market helper
text: You are helping at a fruit and vegetable stand at a weekend farmers market. Listen to the farmer who runs the stand and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: We set up at six.
explanation: Link 'set up at' into 'seh-dup-at' and stress 'six'.

stem: Put the strawberries at the front.
explanation: Say 'strawberries' with stress on 'straw', and keep 'at the front' at the end.

stem: Tomatoes cost three dollars a pound this week.
explanation: In American English 'tomatoes' is 'tuh-MAY-toes'; say 'three dollars a pound' as one price phrase.

stem: Customers who bring their own bags get a small discount.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who bring their own bags' after 'Customers', and stress 'discount' on the first syllable.

stem: Keep the honey jars in the shade so they don't get sticky.
explanation: Link 'honey jars' and stress 'shade'; 'so they don't' is a purpose clause, so keep it at the end.

stem: If someone asks whether the apples are organic, tell them we don't use any pesticides.
explanation: Keep 'whether the apples are organic' in statement order; stress 'organic' on the second syllable.

stem: When the market closes at one, pack the leftover peaches carefully because a restaurant on Elm Street buys them.
explanation: Start with the time clause 'When the market closes at one', and keep the street name 'Elm Street' in the final clause.

title: Campus IT help desk
text: You have started working at the campus computer help desk. Listen to the technical supervisor and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Log every request in the system.
explanation: Link 'log every' smoothly and stress 'every' and 'system'.

stem: Most problems are fixed by restarting the computer.
explanation: Keep the passive 'are fixed by' together, and stress 'restarting' on the second syllable.

stem: The network password changes on the first of each month.
explanation: The w in 'password' is silent; say 'first of each month' as one phrase.

stem: Students who forget their login details can reset them on the portal.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who forget their login details' together, and link 'reset them'.

stem: Never ask a user for their password, even if they offer to tell you.
explanation: Stress 'never' strongly, and keep the 'even if' clause at the end of the sentence.

stem: If a laptop won't turn on, check the charger and the outlet before you open a ticket.
explanation: Say 'won't' with a rounded o so it is not heard as 'want', and keep the final 'before' clause.

stem: Printers in the engineering building often run out of paper during exam week, so take an extra box when you go there.
explanation: Link 'run out of' into one phrase, and keep 'during exam week' before the 'so' clause.

title: Electronics store training
text: You have a new job at an electronics store. Listen to the sales manager and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Greet customers as they come in.
explanation: Link 'come in' into 'kuh-min' and stress 'greet'.

stem: Phone cases are on the left wall.
explanation: Say the plural 'cases' with two syllables, and stress 'left wall'.

stem: Every laptop on display must stay plugged in all day.
explanation: Watch the cluster in 'plugged in' and keep 'on display' after 'laptop'.

stem: Customers can return most items within thirty days with a receipt.
explanation: The p in 'receipt' is silent; say 'within thirty days' as one time phrase.

stem: If someone wants to compare two cameras, show them the chart by the register.
explanation: Keep the 'if' clause first and the place phrase 'by the register' at the end.

stem: The headphones that are on sale this week are kept in the glass case near the entrance.
explanation: Hold the long subject 'The headphones that are on sale this week' together before the verb 'are kept'.

stem: When a customer asks about a repair, take down their phone number and tell them a technician will call within two days.
explanation: Begin with the time clause, link 'take down', and keep 'within two days' at the very end.

title: National park visitor center
text: You are working for the summer at the visitor center of a national park. Listen to the park ranger and repeat what he says. Repeat only once.

stem: Trail maps are free for everyone.
explanation: Stress 'trail maps' and 'free'; 'are' is weak and quick.

stem: The north entrance closes at sunset tonight.
explanation: Watch the th in 'north' and link 'closes at' smoothly.

stem: Remind hikers to carry at least two liters of water.
explanation: Say 'at least' with a clear final t, and stress 'two liters'.

stem: The waterfall trail is steep, so it isn't good for small children.
explanation: Say 'waterfall' with a soft American t, 'WAH-der-fall', and stress 'isn't'.

stem: Campers who want a fire permit can get one at this desk until five.
explanation: Keep the relative clause 'who want a fire permit' together, and keep 'until five' at the end.

stem: If visitors see a bear, they should stay calm, back away slowly, and never run.
explanation: Say the three actions in order with a slight pause between them, and stress 'never'.

stem: The ranger talk about the park's geology starts at two o'clock in the small theater behind this building.
explanation: Keep the possessive 'park's', stress 'geology' on the second syllable, and end with the place phrase 'behind this building'.

title: Coffee shop barista
text: You are starting as a barista at a coffee shop on a university campus. Listen to the shift manager and repeat what she says. Repeat only once.

stem: Clean the milk jugs after use.
explanation: Watch the l in 'milk' and link 'after use' smoothly.

stem: The morning rush starts around seven thirty.
explanation: Stress 'morning rush' and say the time 'seven thirty' clearly.

stem: Write each customer's name on the side of the cup.
explanation: Keep the possessive 'customer's', and say 'side of the cup' as one phrase.

stem: Oat milk and almond milk are in the fridge under the counter.
explanation: The l in 'almond' is usually silent in American English, 'AH-mund'; keep 'under the counter' at the end.

stem: Students who bring a reusable cup get twenty-five cents off any drink.
explanation: Say 'twenty-five cents' as one unit and keep the relative clause 'who bring a reusable cup' together.

stem: When the pastry delivery arrives, check the boxes against the order list before you sign for it.
